key_insight: The paper shows that pairing interpretable machine learning with data storytelling can make AI decisions easier for non-experts to understand without exposing sensitive data or model internals.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for building user-facing AI systems in healthcare, finance, public policy, and other high-stakes settings where explanations must be both understandable and privacy-preserving.
method: Defines data storytelling for interpretable machine learning using the DIST Pyramid.
Introduces an I-P-O model plus an architecture for "What-if" and "Why-not" explanation generation.
Uses data desensitization, SHAP, and LLMs to turn model outputs into ABT-style narratives.
evidence_signal: In a Boston Housing case study, 76.4% and 74.3% of respondents found the "What-if" and "Why-not" stories more comprehensible, with significantly higher accessibility scores than standard SHAP visualizations.
watch_item: Narrative generation with LLMs may introduce wording drift or oversimplification, so explanation fidelity and privacy safeguards need careful validation.
paper_title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details
